topic: Thread Unpredictability: Task Execution Location and Timing
explanation: When using `std::async` with the default policy, it is impossible to predict two critical aspects of the task execution: timing and location. If the task is deferred, it will not run concurrently with the calling thread (`t`). Furthermore, if the task is deferred, it will run synchronously on the very thread that eventually calls `fut.get()` or `fut.wait()`. This ambiguity complicates debugging and timing analysis because a function intended to run concurrently might unexpectedly block the main thread.
practical_example: A program relies on a task starting immediately to meet a deadline. If the task is launched deferred, the delay between the `std::async` call and the subsequent `get()`/`wait()` call counts against the main thread's performance, potentially causing a performance bottleneck where concurrent execution was expected.
chapter: Item 36: Understand std::async behavior under default launch policy
